input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 8.1 sets a three-year term and Section 9 provides only cause-based termination rights (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/service-level/legal/IP failures) — Section 9 skips from 9.3 to 9.5 and contains no convenience right. Section 2.1 goes further and expressly strips Customer of "termination rights" for a three-year take-or-pay commitment. Under the playbook, absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation. We therefore add a new 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no penalty, confirm Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right, and conform Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language does not defeat that right. Vendor is given no convenience right anywhere in the document, so no deletion is needed on that side.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall owe no early-termination fee or other penalty. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction rights, provided that the commitment is reduced pro rata for, and does not limit, any termination by Customer under Section 9.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirmed Vendor has no reciprocal walk-away right during a term, as our playbook requires in any term longer than 12 months. We have also conformed the take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 so it does not override that right; if helpful we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Customer-only termination for convenience (30 days, pro-rata refund) and align Section 2.1 take-or-pay.
